t: This is Waterlow Park, twenty-six acres of green in the southeast corner of Highgate Village, just west of Swain's Lane. The park carries the name of Sir Sydney Waterlow, a philanthropist and Liberal politician. In 1889 he gave it to the public, describing it as a garden for the gardenless. That phrase is what he's best remembered for, and it still sums up what the park is for: open space, free to everyone, in north London.
